messages:
mika: Quick Q — for /v1/generate, should malformed client inputs return 400 or 422? We have a few clients that currently retry on 422 and it's causing weird duplicate submits.
joel: my rule of thumb: 4xx = client must fix, not retryable. 422 is okay for semantic validation but still a 4xx and should be considered non-retryable by SDKs.
san: FWIW some of our JS SDKs treat 422 same as 429 atm (bug). We should standardize before we flip anything server-side.
cassie: propose we formalize an error envelope with an explicit retryable flag + stable codes. Example suggestion (to include in API spec):
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation",
    "code": "invalid_input",
    "message": "missing field 'context'",
    "retryable": false,
    "fields": [{"name":"context","reason":"required"}],
    "doc": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#invalid_input"
  }
}
```
Also: use 429 for rate limits (retryable=true) with a Retry-After header, and 503 for transient infra with retryable=true. For pure validation problems return 400 or 422 (we should pick one and be consistent).
joel: +1 to the explicit "retryable" boolean. SDKs should prefer header Retry-After for backoff timing and fall back to exponential jitter.
mika: Backcompat note: we shouldn't suddenly turn previous 400s into 5xx/429 — that would break customers. If we add fields to the body it's safe as clients should just ignore unknown fields.
san: Actionable plan:1) eng-platform middleware to ensure all error responses include {error.retryable, error.code, error.doc} 2) open PR to update JS + Python SDKs to treat retryable:true as retry candidates, and not retry on 4xx where retryable:false. 3) update OpenAPI examples. I'll start a PR for (1).
deploy-bot: ci: build/1978 passed :white_check_mark: (lint + unit tests)
cassie: For streaming endpoints — special case: we agreed earlier to not return mid-stream non-200 errors when we can avoid it. If we hit token limits mid-stream, return final chunk with "finish_reason":"length" (no error). Only surface errors as non-200 if the whole request failed pre-stream.
joel: good catch. Also: add an error.code namespace so we can add new semantics without breaking (e.g., invalid_input, rate_limit, quota_exceeded, internal_error).
mika: One more edge: should clients ever retry on 409? If conflict can be retried with idempotency keys it might be ok. I propose we mark non-idempotent endpoints as non-retryable on 409 and allow retryable:true on idempotent ops.
san: agree. I'll include an "idempotency" hint in the spec for endpoints and set retryable accordingly.
cassie: SDK guidance snippet: if error.retryable === true -> attempt up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (base 300ms) unless Retry-After header present. Otherwise surface to user. We'll add this to SDK docs.
mika: ok can someone draft the RFC blurb for eng-platform and product to sign off? Keep it short.
san: I'll draft and ping here tomorrow morning. tagging @joel for review. :thumbsup:
joel: will review early. Thanks all.
